# Feature Specification: Returns / Refunds / Voids

**Feature ID:** 014-returns-refunds-voids
**Status:** Draft (SEED — generated by spec-seed workflow; NOT yet through /speckit-specify)
**Created:** 2026-06-07
**Last Updated:** 2026-06-07
**Owner:** (unassigned)

---

## Overview

> **BLOCKED SKELETON — DO NOT IMPLEMENT.**
>
> This feature depends on the **POS-011 sale-sync runtime being LIVE** (a return cannot be posted
> against a sale the backend has never received), **AND** on the Retail-Tower-ERP-Next-Connector's
> reversal-posting path being implemented (currently FAIL-CLOSED / unimplemented). Neither
> precondition is met as of 2026-06-07. This spec is a credible planning skeleton only.

Cashier-initiated returns, refunds, and voids of prior sales at the POS terminal. The workflow
models three reversal kinds:

- **Void** — cancel a sale before it is finalized (same session, pre-sync). No backend record
  exists yet; the terminal discards the pending sale locally.
- **Return / Refund** — reverse a finalized, synced sale. The cashier locates the original sale,
  selects full or partial line-item quantities to return, and the terminal emits append-only
  reversal events to DP2 (`recordVoid` / `recordRefund` in `pos-sales/sales.yaml`). DP2
  orchestrates the downstream Credit Note against ERPNext POS Invoice (status: Credit Note Issued;
  negative-qty Credit Note pattern matching ERPNext's reference model).

The terminal is event-source only: it appends reversal events keyed to the original sale
identifier. It does not mutate its own finalized sale records beyond marking them as reversed.
Tender refund mechanics (cash back, card reversal) are out of scope for capture v1; the event
payload carries the reversal attribution but no tender instruction.

All reversal events are idempotent by original-sale key + reversal-request UUID so that
network retries cannot double-post.

---

## User Scenarios & Testing

### Primary User Story

As a cashier, I need to void an unfinished sale or reverse a finalized sale so that the customer
receives credit and the books reflect the correct transaction history, without requiring me to
re-enter the original items manually.

### Acceptance Scenarios

**Given** a sale has been started but not yet finalized,
**When** the cashier selects Void on the active cart,
**Then** the terminal discards all pending cart lines, resets to an empty cart, and records a
local void event (no backend call is made, because no sale was ever synced).

---

**Given** a finalized and synced sale exists (011 runtime live),
**When** the cashier initiates a full return by locating the original sale and confirming all
line items,
**Then** the terminal emits a `recordRefund` event to DP2 with negative quantities for every
line, keyed to the original sale ID, and displays a success confirmation; the original sale is
marked as reversed in the local read model.

---

**Given** a finalized and synced sale exists,
**When** the cashier initiates a partial return for a subset of line items or reduced quantities,
**Then** the terminal emits a `recordRefund` event covering only the selected items/quantities,
the original sale is marked partially-reversed, and subsequent partial returns are bounded by
the remaining un-returned quantity per line.

---

### Edge Cases

- **Retry / duplicate submit:** a second identical reversal request (same original-sale ID +
  reversal UUID) must be rejected or de-duplicated; the terminal must surface an
  already-reversed status rather than posting twice.
- **Sale not yet synced:** if 011's sync queue shows the original sale as pending (not yet
  acknowledged by DP2), the cashier must receive a clear blocking message — reversal is
  unavailable until sync is confirmed.
- **Connector reversal FAIL-CLOSED:** if DP2 returns a non-success status from the Connector's
  reversal path, the terminal must surface the failure without silently marking the sale reversed.
- **Partial return limits:** attempting to return more quantity than was sold (or more than
  remains unreturned) must be rejected with a user-visible validation message before submission.
- **Offline:** reversal requires a live DP2 connection; the terminal must block the action and
  display an offline notice rather than queuing a reversal event for later replay.

---

## Requirements

### Functional Requirements

**FR-1 — Void before finalize:** The terminal must allow the cashier to void any active,
unfinalized cart. Voiding discards all cart lines, emits a local void audit record, and does
not call DP2 (no sale was synced).

**FR-2 — Locate prior sale:** The terminal must provide a look-up surface to find a finalized
sale by receipt number or terminal-assigned sale ID, displaying summary (date, total, line
items) before the cashier commits to a return.

**FR-3 — Full return:** The cashier must be able to select all line items for return in a single
operation. The terminal confirms the selection, then emits a `recordRefund` event to DP2 with
negative quantities for every line.

**FR-4 — Partial return:** The cashier must be able to select a subset of line items, or reduce
the quantity of individual lines, and return only those items. Returned quantities are bounded
by original quantity minus previously returned quantity.

**FR-5 — Idempotent submission:** Every reversal request must carry a terminal-generated
idempotency UUID. DP2 must not be called a second time if a reversal with the same UUID is
already recorded as accepted.

**FR-6 — Sync-gate check:** Before emitting any reversal event, the terminal must verify that
the original sale is in a synced/acknowledged state via 011's sync-state store. If the sale is
pending or failed, the reversal action must be blocked with a user-visible explanation.

**FR-7 — Reversal attribution and audit:** Every reversal event payload must include the
original sale ID, the reversing cashier's session token, the terminal ID, and the UTC timestamp.
PII and card data must never appear in any log or event payload.

**FR-8 — Local read-model update:** On confirmed acceptance from DP2, the terminal must update
its local sale record to reflect reversed / partially-reversed status so that subsequent
look-ups display the correct state.

**FR-9 — Failure surface:** If DP2 returns an error (including Connector FAIL-CLOSED), the
terminal must display a human-readable failure message and leave the sale's local status
unchanged. Silent failure is not permitted.

**FR-10 — Offline guard:** If the terminal is offline at the time of reversal initiation, the
action must be blocked immediately with an offline notice. Reversal events must not be queued
for deferred replay.

### Non-Functional Requirements

**NFR-1 — Idempotency window:** The terminal must retain reversal UUIDs for at least 24 hours
to prevent duplicate posts across reconnection cycles.

**NFR-2 — Response time:** The reversal submission round-trip (terminal → DP2 → terminal
confirmation) must complete within 5 seconds on a normal clinic network; the UI must show a
loading indicator during the call.

**NFR-3 — Audit completeness:** Every void and reversal operation (including blocked/failed
attempts) must produce a local audit log entry that survives terminal restart.

---

## Success Criteria

**SC-1** — A cashier can void an unfinalized cart without any DP2 call, and the terminal returns
to an empty cart state.

**SC-2** — A cashier can locate a finalized synced sale, select all or a subset of lines, submit
the return, and receive a success confirmation; DP2's `recordRefund` endpoint is called exactly
once per unique reversal UUID.

**SC-3** — A duplicate submission (same reversal UUID) is de-duplicated; DP2 is not called a
second time.

**SC-4** — Attempting to return more quantity than is available surfaces a validation error
before any network call is made.

**SC-5** — Attempting a reversal against an un-synced sale is blocked with a clear message.

**SC-6** — A DP2 error response leaves local sale status unchanged and displays a failure message
to the cashier.

**SC-7** — All reversal payloads contain attribution fields (cashier session, terminal ID, UTC
timestamp, original sale ID) and contain no PII or card data.

---

## Key Entities

| Entity | Description |
|:--|:--|
| `Sale` | A finalized, locally persisted sale record (owned by 011's sync-state store). Carries sync status (pending / synced / failed). |
| `ReversalRequest` | Ephemeral terminal-side object representing the cashier's selection: original sale ID, line items + quantities, reversal UUID, cashier session reference. |
| `ReversalEvent` | The append-only payload emitted to DP2 via `recordVoid` / `recordRefund`. Keyed by original sale ID + reversal UUID. |
| `VoidAuditRecord` | Local-only record for a pre-finalize void (no backend event). Retained for audit. |
| `SyncState` | 011's per-sale sync-status store; read by this feature to gate reversals. |

---

## Assumptions

- DP2 `recordVoid` and `recordRefund` endpoints (`pos-sales/sales.yaml`) are the sole write
  surface; the terminal does not call ERPNext or the Connector directly.
- The ERPNext Credit Note pattern (negative-qty against original POS Invoice, status Credit Note
  Issued) is the downstream model; the terminal is unaware of it — DP2 and the Connector handle
  the mapping.
- Tender refund disbursement (returning cash, reversing a card charge) is handled outside the
  terminal in v1 and is not part of this feature.
- Restock / inventory adjustment on return is handled downstream by the Connector and is not
  the terminal's concern.
- The cashier has an active authenticated operator session (004) before initiating any reversal.
- 011's sync-state store is readable by the returns feature without cross-feature coupling
  beyond a well-defined read interface.

---

## Out of Scope

- Tender refund mechanics (cash back, card reversal, change calculation).
- Inventory restock or stock-adjustment events.
- Manager-approval workflows or dual-authorisation for returns.
- Return reason codes or disposition tracking.
- Offline / queued reversal replay (reversals require a live DP2 connection).
- ERPNext or Connector code changes (those are downstream of DP2).
- Automated exchange (return + new sale in one flow).

---

## Dependencies

> **BLOCKING (hard):** This feature cannot be implemented or tested end-to-end until:
>
> 1. **POS-011 sale-sync runtime is LIVE.** A return event references an original sale that must
>    already exist in DP2's records. Until 011's capture-UP runtime is operational, no synced
>    sale exists to reverse.
> 2. **Retail-Tower-ERP-Next-Connector reversal-posting path is implemented.** The Connector
>    currently FAIL-CLOSES on reversal posts (unimplemented). DP2 `recordRefund` will fail
>    end-to-end until the Connector handles it.

| Dependency | Kind | Status |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **POS-011 sale-sync runtime** | BLOCKING | Not yet live |
| **Connector reversal-posting** | BLOCKING | Unimplemented (FAIL-CLOSED) |
| DP2 `recordVoid` / `recordRefund` endpoints (`pos-sales/sales.yaml`) | Contract (partial) | Endpoints exist + implemented in DP2; Connector leg blocked |
| POS-004 Operator Session | Runtime | Complete |
| POS-008 Sale Finalization | Upstream data | Complete |
| POS-005 Sales Cart | Upstream data | Complete |

## Open Questions

**[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: 011-runtime + Connector-reversal sequencing]** POS-011's capture-UP
runtime and the Connector's reversal-posting path are both required before any end-to-end
test of this feature is possible. What is the expected delivery timeline for each, and should
014 be formally sequenced behind a 011 gate in the roadmap?

**[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: partial-return idempotency surface]** Should the terminal enforce
partial-return quantity limits purely locally (read from the local sale record), or does DP2
expose a remaining-returnable-quantity endpoint? If local-only, concurrent returns from two
terminals against the same sale may race.

**[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: void audit retention]** Pre-finalize voids never produce a DP2 event.
What is the required local retention period for `VoidAuditRecord`, and must it be surfaced in
any operator-facing audit report?
